newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico faked evidence against Raul Salinas - wife.
newsitem.headline: Mexico faked evidence against Raul Salinas - wife.

text.p: Mexican prosecutors have faked evidence, bribed witnesses and distorted facts in their attempt to prove that former President Carlos Salinas' brother Raul ordered the murder of a top politician, Raul Salinas' wife alleged in an interview published on Monday.

Paulina Castanon told the newspaper Reforma from Switzerland, where she is testifying in an investigation, that she was convinced Raul was innocent of the September 1994 murder of his former brother-in-law Jose Francisco Ruiz Massieu, secretary general of the ruling party.
"It was incredible they accused him of killing anyone, still less Jose Francisco," she said. "Someone to whom he was linked by so many years of friendship, the father of his nephews."

Salinas' sister Adriana divorced Ruiz Massieu some years before the murder. He was arrested in February 1995, jailed in a top security cell and accused of masterminding Ruiz Massieu's murder, but more than two years later prosecutors have not produced hard evidence to back up their claims.

"There are fabricated documents and witnesses who follow instructions, (who are) threatened and rewarded," Castanon said, adding that lawyers had evidence to back her claims. "But I know that all this will be cleared up and the truth will come out."

Salinas' lawyers say their client has been framed by the government of President Ernesto Zedillo as part of a campaign against the former Salinas administration. Carlos Salinas was hugely popular in office but his reputation crumbled when the economy collapsed weeks after he left office and allegations surfaced of massive corruption.

Castanon was herself arrested in November 1995 in Switzerland. Mexican prosecutors said at the time she was trying to withdraw money from a bank account containing $84 million of her husband's cash registered under a false name.

In Monday's interview, she said Mexican prosecutors had even lied about the circumstances of that detention. "I did not think, at any time, about withdrawing money," she said. "I did not have fake documents or false passports. The story the attorney general's office gave was false."
Castanon was held for a month in Switzerland but was freed without charge. On returning to Mexico, she said she was warned by prosecutors not to talk to the press.
